description: An eight step sequencer whose step values come from jacks rather than knobs, with four rows read at the same step

params.text: Advances the sequence one step each press
Returns the sequence to step one
Sets how many of the eight steps are played before the sequence returns to step one, a whole number from 1 to 8

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V advances the sequence one step
A rising edge above 1V returns the sequence to step one
Replaces the steps knob while it is patched, one step per volt counted from zero, and held between 1 and 8
The value the a output carries while the sequence is on that step
The value the b output carries while the sequence is on that step
The value the c output carries while the sequence is on that step
The value the d output carries while the sequence is on that step

outputs.text: Whatever is patched into the a row's jack for the step the sequence is on
Whatever is patched into the b row's jack for the step the sequence is on
Whatever is patched into the c row's jack for the step the sequence is on
Whatever is patched into the d row's jack for the step the sequence is on
The four rows on one poly cable, a on channel 1, b on channel 2, c on channel 3 and d on channel 4, all for the step the sequence is on

notes: A row gives out 0V on any step whose jack has nothing patched into it
The step count is read only when a clock pulse arrives, so changing it takes effect at the next pulse
A reset and a clock arriving together give the reset: the step does not advance on that sample

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the steps knob; a negative voltage does nothing here.
